texts: On day 1 of Year 1, Pell collected silken threads from the lanterns of the Cliff Path at dawn.
Nightmoths had landed on the lanterns during the night.
The nightmoths had left silken threads on the lanterns.
Pell carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper filled the three cauldrons with sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in the sea-water.
Mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in three clay vessels.

q1_issues.issue: The nightmoth group sk_nightmoth_1 is the subject of two distributive predicates (land, leave) but gets only the group event, with no per-member (Implication (PartOf $x sk_nightmoth_1) ...) distribution rule of the kind Quantifiers/Cardinality require for a grouped plural with a distributive predicate.

review.notes: The instruction set is itself in tension here: the bare-plural-episodic passage describes only a group witness acting in a normal event ("rescuers reached the ridge"), while Quantifiers/Cardinality say a grouped plural with a distributive predicate adds the per-member rule. Minor: sk_thread_1 is reused for the bare-plural re-mention "silken threads" in sentence 3, which is discourse-coherent but is strictly a fresh indefinite introduction.

issues.reason: Coordination & plurals states that a distributive predicate "also hands the predication to the group's members via a rule", and Quantifiers names a "grouped / counted plural" ("the dogs barked") as taking the per-member (PartOf $x <group>) rule beside the group event, so the nightmoth group's landing and leaving each owe a rule the parse never emits.

new_gaps: A plural-headed multi-word proper name ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools"): Names and casing licenses one singular type atom for a kind word inside a name (Kestrel River -> river) and bars GroupOf / per-member kind on a plural name-label ("the Wrens"), so nothing licenses recording that the named referent is a SET of tide-pools - (Member salt_bloom_tide_pools tide_pool) is the only form on offer and it types a plurality as one pool.
adjudication.defect_summary: Compliant form: beside each nightmoth group event, the per-member distribution rule over the group - (: nm_land (Implication (PartOf $x sk_nightmoth_1) (And (Member (sk_land $x) land) (Agent (sk_land $x) $x) (Location (sk_land $x) sk_lantern_1) (Time (sk_land $x) night) (Past (sk_land $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9)) and the parallel (sk_leave $x) rule carrying (Theme ... sk_thread_1) and (Location ... sk_lantern_1); the group events and Before atoms stay as they are.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the passage holds up against the instruction set: the silken_thread / nightmoth / sea_water / tide_pool / clay_vessel decompositions obey the noun-modifier bar, "by evening" is correctly TimeAtMost on a day-part, entity-attached From carries the sea-water's origin, and both past perfects get their Before against an asserted event. The reviewer was right to leave the sk_thread_1 reuse unfiled - the threads in sentence 3 are the ones already introduced, and Coreference licenses symbol reuse for a later mention of an introduced referent.
